chunks: Abu Hammam wrote to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who rented an estate from another man, then the lessor sold that estate in the presence of the tenant, and the tenant did not object to the sale and was present for it as a witness to it. Then the buyer died and left heirs. Does that property return as part of the deceased's inheritance, or does it remain in the hand of the tenant until his lease expires?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "It remains in the hand of the tenant until his lease expires."

key_terms.إِجَارَتُهُ: his lease term or rental contract
key_terms.الْبَيْعَ: the sale transaction of the property
key_terms.الْمُؤَاجِرُ: the lessor or landlord who leased out the property
key_terms.الْمُسْتَأْجِرِ: the tenant or lessee who holds the lease
key_terms.ضَيْعَةً: an estate or landed property that is being leased
key_terms.مِيرَاثِ: the inheritance estate of the deceased

ai.seo_question: If a rented property is sold and the buyer later dies, does the tenant keep possession until the lease ends?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about leased property that is sold during the lease term. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the tenant's right of possession remains valid until the agreed lease period ends, even if the buyer dies and leaves heirs.
